Posterior count of the latent factors a model uses

Source: R/active_factors.R
active_factors.Rd

A factor model fitted with n_lv factors may need fewer. This function counts the factors whose variance the data support. It suits a fit under the multiplicative gamma process (MGP) prior, loadings_prior = "mgp" (Bhattacharya and Dunson 2011). That prior shrinks surplus factors toward zero. n_lv then acts as a ceiling. The function applies to every factor model. Under other loadings priors a surplus factor keeps the variance its prior gives it. The count can then exceed the number of factors the data need.

Usage

active_factors(object, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
active_factors(
  object,
  criterion = c("relative", "cumulative"),
  threshold = NULL,
  prob = 0.5,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam object whose trend includes at least two latent factors (n_lv >= 2).

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

criterion

The activity rule: "relative" (the default) or "cumulative". Details describes each.

threshold

Numeric in (0, 1], the cut-off of criterion. NULL (the default) takes 0.1 for "relative" and 0.9 for "cumulative".

prob

Numeric in (0, 1). A dimension is reported active when its posterior probability of activity is at least prob. Defaults to 0.5.

Value

A list with class mvgam_active_factors containing:

  • count: the posterior median, q025 and q975 of the per-draw count of active dimensions.

  • per_factor: data frame with one row per dimension, largest first. Its columns are the factor rank, the posterior prob_active, the posterior median_variance \(\lambda_k\), the posterior median_share of the total variance and is_active.

  • threshold: list with criterion, value and prob.

  • n_lv: the number of factors the model was fitted with.

Details

The factors give the series the covariance \(Z \Omega Z^\top\), where Z holds the loadings and \(\Omega\) the covariance of the latent states. Its eigenvalues \(\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \dots\) are the variances along its principal dimensions. Each posterior draw gives one set. The eigenvalues stay the same when the factors are rotated or relabelled, which the individual columns of Z do not.

Two rules decide whether dimension k is active in a draw:

"relative"

The dimension holds at least threshold times the variance of the leading one, \(\lambda_k \ge\) threshold \(\lambda_1\). The default threshold is 0.1. The rule counts any number of factors of similar size.

"cumulative"

The dimension is among the fewest leading dimensions whose variance reaches a share threshold of the total. The default threshold is 0.9. The count is the number of factors a scree plot would keep.

prob_active is the posterior probability that a dimension is active. A dimension with prob_active >= prob is reported active. The count is summarised over the per-draw counts.

Both rules compare the factors with one another. The leading dimension is always active, which makes the count at least one. A model whose factors hold almost no variance still reports one. shared_variation() gives the size of that variance on the scale of the linear predictor.

References

Bhattacharya, A. and Dunson, D. B. (2011). Sparse Bayesian infinite factor models. Biometrika, 98(2), 291-306. doi:10.1093/biomet/asr013 .

See also

shared_variation() reports the covariance the factors give the series. compare_loadings() compares the loadings under two priors. The JSDM article fits an MGP prior and counts its active factors.

Other latent dynamics: compare_loadings(), fevd.mvgam(), irf.mvgam(), ordinate(), posterior_transition_matrix(), residual_cor(), shared_variation(), stability.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
# Counts of 20 species at 100 sites, driven by two latent factors.
# Each species has its own intercept and response to `env`.
simdat <- sim_jsdgam(family = brms::negbinomial(), n_species = 20L,
                     n_sites = 100L, n_lv = 2L, seed = 3L)

# Up to five factors under the MGP prior, which shrinks the factors
# the data do not need
mod <- jsdgam(
  y ~ env * series,
  data           = simdat$data_train,
  family         = brms::negbinomial(),
  n_lv           = 5L,
  loadings_prior = "mgp",
  chains         = 2,
  silent         = 2
)

# Dimensions holding at least a tenth of the leading one's variance
af <- active_factors(mod)
af
#> Active latent factors
#>   Rule: variance at least 0.1 times the leading factor's
#>   Fitted with: n_lv = 5
#>   Posterior median active count: 2.0 (95% CI 2.0 - 3.0)
#> 
#> Posterior probability that each factor is active, largest first:
#>  factor prob_active median_variance median_share is_active
#>       1       1.000          9.3600        0.661      TRUE
#>       2       1.000          4.0200        0.284      TRUE
#>       3       0.110          0.5390        0.038     FALSE
#>       4       0.001          0.1480        0.010     FALSE
#>       5       0.000          0.0366        0.003     FALSE
plot(af)


# The fewest dimensions that explain 90 percent of the variance
active_factors(mod, criterion = "cumulative")
#> Active latent factors
#>   Rule: fewest factors reaching a 0.9 share of the variance
#>   Fitted with: n_lv = 5
#>   Posterior median active count: 2.0 (95% CI 2.0 - 3.0)
#> 
#> Posterior probability that each factor is active, largest first:
#>  factor prob_active median_variance median_share is_active
#>       1       1.000          9.3600        0.661      TRUE
#>       2       1.000          4.0200        0.284      TRUE
#>       3       0.054          0.5390        0.038     FALSE
#>       4       0.000          0.1480        0.010     FALSE
#>       5       0.000          0.0366        0.003     FALSE

# Next: ordinate() plots the species on the leading factors
# }
